<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via OS_ORG_INVITATION_LIMIT (literal, a string literal in resolveOrgInvitationLimit))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **31** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f9d90c85b2aa51aa2812aad48fe8cb409a9a7aaa` — the merge of head `f13394bc5b5b5e782c63d302dbc4635124830524` into base `67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f9d90c85b2aa51aa2812aad48fe8cb409a9a7aaa && git checkout f9d90c85b2aa51aa2812aad48fe8cb409a9a7aaa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907 f13394bc5b5b5e782c63d302dbc4635124830524 && git checkout -B drift-repro 67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907 && git merge --no-ff f13394bc5b5b5e782c63d302dbc4635124830524

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `37a7086e614eeefaa07142a472b709ef61177e9e`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #33196 (body, triage, claim, claim amendment, os-dev-report), PR #33208 (body, 7-file list, `git diff origin/main...pr33208`), and the head's 45 check-runs. Code outside the diff was read to judge it and is not reviewed here. That includes better-auth 1.7.12 `dist/plugins/organization/{types.d.mts,routes/crud-invites.mjs,adapter.mjs}`, read from the published 1.7.12 tarball because this checkout has no `node_modules`; the lockfile pins `better-auth@1.7.12`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Gates at review time (03:05Z).** 14 success, 9 skipped (all opt-in or event-gated: Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, the dogfood shard matrix, UI Published Artifacts, Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict, Schedule gate), 0 failed. Still in progress and not judged: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Build Docs, Live E2E UI, Type Check (workspace, source gates, debt ledger, consumer gates), Lint (ESLint, docs and code guards, repo and tooling gates, CI/release/engine gates, both scoped legs). Concluded green and relevant here: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Dogfood Regression Gate. This verdict holds only if the in-progress runs conclude green. A red one reopens it.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff changes these accept sets and public surfaces:

1. **`POST /api/v1/auth/organization/invite-member`, the pending-invitation ceiling. Right.** The vendor code (crud-invites.mjs L167-172) is `invitationLimit = typeof opt === "function" ? await opt(...) : opt ?? 100`, then `if (pending.length >= invitationLimit) throw FORBIDDEN INVITATION_LIMIT_REACHED`. `pending` comes from `findPendingInvitations`, which keeps rows with `status = 'pending'` for this `organizationId` and then drops any whose `expiresAt` has passed (adapter.mjs L772-782). The count is per organization, and expired rows do not count. The diff's three legs:
   - **Unset, blank, `0`, negative or non-numeric: no key, so the vendor's 100 applies. Right, and the option object is identical to main's.** `resolveInvitationLimitOption()` returns `undefined`. `...(invitationLimit === undefined ? {} : { invitationLimit })` spreads an empty object, so the `organizationOptions` literal has the same keys and values as on main. The new call reads one env var through `readEnvWithDeprecation(..., [], { silent: true })`, the same path its neighbours use: no log and no side effect. On main the vendor reads `undefined ?? 100`, and it still does.
   - **A positive integer N: `invitationLimit: N`. Right.** With N pending, the next invitation is refused with 403. This matches the docs row ("may hold N at once").
   - **`off`, `unlimited` or `none`, trimmed and in any case: `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. Right.** The vendor type is `number | ((data, ctx) => Awaitable of number) | undefined` (types.d.mts L156). A number is accepted, and `length >= 9007199254740991` is never true in practice. The value is finite, which matches `MEMBERSHIP_LIMIT_UNBOUNDED`. Option-shape alternatives, as the vendor reads them: `null` falls back to 100 through `??`; `0` refuses everything; `Infinity` would also work.
2. **Parser edge cases (`resolveOrgInvitationLimit`, which trims, checks the off list, then `parseInt(value, 10)` and `n > 0`).**
   - These read as unset, which is the safe side: `-1`, `-5`, `-0`, `0x10` (parseInt gives 0), `NaN`, `Infinity`/`infinity` (NaN, so unset rather than off; the docs file it under unparsable), `false`, `abc`, blank, whitespace only.
   - These parse as expected: `' 7 '` gives 7, `+5` gives 5, `OFF`/`None`/`' unlimited '` give off.
   - A huge value such as `99999999999999999999` gives `1e20`. That is finite and positive, so it is passed and is in effect unlimited. Harmless.
   - **Wrong against the docs. See the should-fix in ③.** `parseInt` reads the leading integer, so `1e3` gives **1**, `2.5` gives 2, `1_000` gives 1 and `100abc` gives 100. The docs row and the changeset both promise that "anything unparsable reads as unset (100), so a typo never refuses every invitation". `OS_ORG_INVITATION_LIMIT=1e3`, a plausible way to write a thousand, sets a limit of **1**: once one invitation is pending, every further one is refused. This idiom is the one `resolveOrgLimit` and `resolveOrgMembershipLimit` already use, so the export is consistent with its neighbours. But the neighbours' docs do not promise typo safety in these words, and this row does. Nothing pins `1e3` or a float.
3. **The new `@objectstack/types` exports `resolveOrgInvitationLimit(): number | 'off' | undefined` and `ORG_INVITATION_LIMIT_OFF_VALUES`. Right.** They are reached through `export * from './env.js'` in index.ts, and they use the same reader, the same `{ silent: true }` and the same `parseInt`/`n > 0` rule as `resolveOrgLimit` and `resolveOrgMembershipLimit`. The extra `'off'` arm in the return type is justified. For membership, unset already means unbounded, so that function needs no separate off value. Here unset must keep 100, so off has to be told apart from unset, and an `'off'` sentinel in the types layer is the minimal way to do that. The plugin-auth wrapper `resolveInvitationLimitOption()` mirrors `resolveMembershipLimitOption()`, and `INVITATION_LIMIT_UNBOUNDED` mirrors `MEMBERSHIP_LIMIT_UNBOUNDED`. Both new exports are additions; nothing is removed or renamed.
4. **Other invitation doors. Right: none applies its own limit.**
   - Every framework invitation surface targets `/api/v1/auth/organization/invite-member`: the actions on sys_invitation, sys_member, sys_organization and sys_user, the resend action, and `@objectstack/client`'s invite.
   - No framework code inserts `sys_invitation` rows outside the vendor (grep of `packages/**` outside tests).
   - The vendor's re-invite/resend branch (crud-invites L142-161) returns before the limit check, so resending an existing pending invitation still works at the limit, as on main.
   - A cloud-managed environment refuses every invitation in `beforeCreateInvitation` (#25083), so the setting has no effect there.
   - The environment-originated door named on the card is cloud#4475, outside this repo. The card makes turning it off the cloud card's step.
5. **What the pins prove. Right: all three legs go through the real plugin.** `invitation-limit.test.ts` builds a real `AuthManager` over the installed better-auth and sends the deciding invitation through the vendor's own `POST /organization/invite-member`. The pending rows are clones of a real first invitation's row, with the same `expiresAt`, so the vendor's count and expiry filter see them.
   - off: the 101st invitation gets 200 and 101 rows are pending.
   - N=3: the 3rd gets 200, and the 4th gets 403 `INVITATION_LIMIT_REACHED` with 3 pending.
   - Unset (control): the 101st gets 403 with the exact body and 100 pending, and the 100th gets 200, so the refusal comes from the limit and not from the harness.
   - The off leg on its own shows only that the limit is above 100. The unit leg pins the exact `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, finite and above 1e6.
   - The types block pins unset, 250, four off spellings, eight unusable values (`''`, whitespace, `abc`, `0`, `-5`, `NaN`, `false`, `infinity`) and independence from `OS_ORG_MEMBERSHIP_LIMIT`.
   - The dev's ablations A1-A4, recorded in the PR body and not re-run here, each turn their own leg red.
6. **The docs row (`environment-variables.mdx`, Authentication table). Right, except for the parse caveat in item 2.** These statements match the vendor and the wiring: the route and the 403 code and message; that a pending invitation leaves the count when it is "accepted, rejected, cancelled or expires" (status leaves `pending`, or the expiry filter drops it); "per organization, not per inviter"; and "read when the auth plugin builds its organization plugin, so a change needs a process reload" (the value is resolved once, before the options literal).
7. **The changeset's description. Right, except for the same parse caveat.** It covers both moved packages and names the new types export.

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/types`. Right.** AGENTS.md (changeset rule 3) ties the level to the Metadata-protocol kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening also ships `patch`. Both packages that publish code changes are listed. `@objectstack/types` is in the `fixed` group, so it moves with its group.
- Both the changeset body and the PR body carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as line-initial declarations. Check Changeset has concluded green.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is right.** The setting is a host env var, not an authorable spec key: `auth-config.zod.ts` and every `packages/spec` path are untouched, and Spec property liveness is green.
- **`widening` is right.** With nothing set, the accept set is unchanged. `off` accepts invitations that main refuses (the 101st and later). Nothing is taken away from any consumer unless the host opts in. A host can choose `N` below 100 and so narrow its own deployment, but that is the host's configuration, not a change the diff imposes. No BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

Findings, graded:

- **should-fix, parse versus promise.** `OS_ORG_INVITATION_LIMIT=1e3` (or `2.5`, `1_000`) parses to its leading integer (1, 2, 1), but the docs row and the changeset say "anything unparsable reads as unset (100), so a typo never refuses every invitation". `1e3` reads as a limit of 1. Two ways to fix it:
  - Accept only `^[0-9]+$` after the trim, so anything else reads as unset, and pin `1e3` and `2.5` as unset in env.test.ts. This diverges from the two neighbours, which is acceptable, and says so.
  - Or keep the shared idiom and make the docs and changeset say "a leading-integer parse: `1e3` reads as 1".
  This does not block. Unset, `off`, N and every pinned bad value behave as stated. The cloud's own step is `off`, which parses exactly.
- **nit, comment accuracy (`invitation-limit.ts` jsdoc, and the PR body's "Why this shape").**
  - "`false` or `null` would fall back to the vendor's 100" is half wrong. The vendor reads `opt ?? 100`, so `null` falls back but `false` does not. `length >= false` compares against 0 and refuses every invitation.
  - "its type is a plain `number`" is also inexact: the vendor type is a number or a function returning one, as the PR body itself says.
  No code path passes `false`, so behaviour is unaffected.
- **nit, test hygiene (`env.test.ts`, "is independent of OS_ORG_MEMBERSHIP_LIMIT").** The test sets `OS_ORG_MEMBERSHIP_LIMIT` and deletes it only after the assertion. A failing assertion leaks the value, and an inherited value is erased rather than restored.

The dev's os-dev-report flags and open questions, answered:

- `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`. Confirmed: no question is left open by the card, and nothing in the diff reaches security or another lane's surface.
- **File surface against the claim and its amendment. In bounds.** The diff touches exactly what the amended claim names: `env.ts` and its test, the new `invitation-limit.ts` and its test, the one wiring spread, the Authentication docs row, and one changeset covering both packages. `auth-config.zod.ts` is untouched, as the amendment said.
- **"CI check-runs pending at report time".** That is still partly true at review time. The open runs are listed above, and nothing has failed.
- **"Gates run at d545f1fb; origin/main merged once (37a7086e), no re-run".** Checked: `d545f1fb..37a7086e` brings only `ui/` paths, `docs/design` paths and one unrelated changeset (`33158-...`). None of them is a file this PR touches. Not re-running was sound, and CI on the head covers the merge.
- **"dogfood_battery: n/a".** Right: the title has no `!`, and the PR declares Clause-② `yes (widening)`, not narrowing.
- **The 101st-refusal premise.** Confirmed against the vendor source above (`?? 100`, `>=`, counted per organization, expiry filtered). The control pin shows main's behaviour is unchanged.
- **The vendor default in the docs ("unset (100)") depends on better-auth's `?? 100`.** If a future better-auth bump changes that default, the unset control pin fails, which is what it is for. No action needed.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f13394bc5b5b5e782c63d302dbc4635124830524`
Local-runs: none

**This is a delta review over record 6870718744**, which reviewed `37a7086e`. It covers one commit, `f13394bc` ("fix(types): read OS_ORG_INVITATION_LIMIT as digits only"), and only `git diff 37a7086e pr33208-r2`. The delta touches five files: `env.ts`, `env.test.ts`, `invitation-limit.ts`, `invitation-limit.test.ts` and `environment-variables.mdx`. Everything record 6870718744 judged outside those files stands. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Gates at review time (03:18Z).**
- **New head `f13394bc`:** 22 check-runs had started. 1 has succeeded (Governed Surface Queue Guard) and 3 were skipped. 6 are in progress: Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, PR-body guards, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check PR Size and Spec property liveness. 12 are queued: every Type Check and Lint leg. Test Core, Test UI and the Build jobs have not started. **None has failed, and no test verdict has concluded.**
- **Old head `37a7086e`:** its runs were cancelled when this commit was pushed, between 03:17:35 and 03:17:46Z. Its two `failure` rows, "TypeScript Type Check" and "Test UI", each completed 2 seconds after starting, right after their children were cancelled. They are roll-up rows over cancelled children, not verdicts on the code.
- This verdict holds only if the new head's runs conclude green. A red one reopens it.

### ① Derived judgments (delta)

1. **SF1, the parse versus the promise. Fixed correctly.**
   - **The check.** `resolveOrgInvitationLimit` now runs `if (!/^\d+$/.test(value)) return undefined` after the trim and the off check, and before `parseInt`. In JavaScript, `\d` without the `u` flag is ASCII `[0-9]` only, and `$` without the `m` flag anchors at the end of the input. The value is already trimmed, so trailing whitespace or a newline cannot slip through.
   - **What now reads as unset:** `1e3`, `2.5`, `1_000`, `10abc`, `-5`, `0x10` and `Infinity`. `0` passes the regex and is then refused by `n > 0`, so it also reads as unset.
   - **What still parses:** `' 7 '` reads 7, `007` reads 7, the off spellings read off, and a long digit string reads a finite number above `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, which is in effect unlimited.
   - **The pins.**
     - The types block adds `1e3`, `2.5`, `1_000` and `10abc` to the unset list, so it now pins twelve unusable values.
     - The plugin-auth unit leg adds `1e3` and `2.5`.
     - Each new pin fails if the check is removed: `parseInt` gives 1, 2, 1 and 10 for those four values.
   - **The docs row.** It now reads "`0`, or any value that is not plain digits (`-5`, `2.5`, `1e3`, `1_000`), reads as unset (100)". That is exactly what the code does.
   - **The changeset.** It is unchanged and still reads "Unset, `0` or an unparsable value keeps today's limit of 100". Under the digit-only rule every non-digit value is unparsable, so the sentence is now true as written.
   - **The jsdoc's answer list.** It names the same values the code refuses.
2. **Nit, the `false` comment. Fixed correctly in the code; one fragment remains.**
   - The jsdoc on `INVITATION_LIMIT_UNBOUNDED` now says the vendor compares "after `invitationLimit ?? 100`", that "`null` would fall back to the vendor's 100", and that "`false` (kept by `??`, compared as 0) and `0` would refuse every invitation". This matches crud-invites.mjs L171-172.
   - Still there, still a nit: the same sentence says the vendor's type is "a plain `number`", but the vendor type is a number or a function returning one (types.d.mts L156).
   - Still there, still a nit: the PR body's "Why this shape" bullet still says "`false` or `null` would fall back to 100", and its Verification section still names `37a7086e`. Neither the comment nor the PR body is published code, and neither changes behaviour.
3. **Nit, restoring the env var in the test. Fixed correctly.** The independence test saves `OS_ORG_MEMBERSHIP_LIMIT` first, runs its assertion inside a `try`, and in the `finally` either deletes the variable (it was unset) or restores the saved value. A failing assertion no longer leaks the value, and an inherited value is no longer erased.
4. **New in this delta: values that changed outcome. They are acceptable and the docs cover them.**
   - Against the previous head:
     - `+5` now reads as unset instead of 5. The docs say "not plain digits", so this is covered.
     - `1e3`, `2.5`, `1_000` and `10abc` now read as unset instead of a limit of 1, 2, 1 and 10.
   - Neither head has been released, and against main the unset path is still identical: no key, so the vendor's 100.
   - The parser now differs from its neighbours `resolveOrgLimit` and `resolveOrgMembershipLimit`, which still use a bare `parseInt`. Record 6870718744 offered that divergence as a fix, and the new code comment explains it.
   - The wiring line, the off and N mappings, `INVITATION_LIMIT_UNBOUNDED` and the integration pins are untouched by the delta.

### ② Semver level (delta)

- **`patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/types` stands.** The delta adds no export, renames nothing and leaves the changeset file unchanged. Its declaration lines `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are still present.
- **`widening` still holds against main.** Unset is unchanged and `off` accepts the 101st invitation. The delta only makes more malformed values read as unset, the safe side.

### ③ Boundary flags (delta)

- **should-fix SF1: closed**, with pins at both layers.
- **nit, `false` comment: closed in the code.** Residual nit, not blocking: "its type is a plain `number`" in the `invitation-limit.ts` jsdoc, and the PR body's unchanged "`false` or `null` would fall back to 100" line and stale `37a7086e` verification head.
- **nit, env test restore: closed.**
- **New must-fix or should-fix in the delta: none.**
- **CI:** no test or typecheck verdict has concluded on `f13394bc` yet, as listed above.

## 维护者速读 · PR #33208 @ `f13394bc` · 2026-11-14T03:48Z

- 改了什么：新增宿主环境变量 `OS_ORG_INVITATION_LIMIT`，控制一个组织最多可以同时挂多少条待接受的邀请。不设、空值或写错（包括 `0`、`-5`、`2.5`、`1e3` 这类不是纯数字的值）时什么都不传，better-auth 照旧用 100；写正整数 N 就是 N；写 `off`、`unlimited` 或 `none`（不分大小写）就不限。
- 为什么改：#33196，依据维护者「邀请上线也接受你的建议」：两个入口都不限待接受邀请数，通过显式的框架设置来关。今天第 101 条待接受邀请会被 `403 INVITATION_LIMIT_REACHED` 拒绝；本 PR 合并后，云端会把它设为 off。
- 权限与边界：不变。谁能发邀请照旧，只是数量上限可以配置。不设这个变量时，传给 better-auth 的组织插件选项与 `main` 完全相同。
- 风险与回滚：新增 `@objectstack/types` 的 `resolveOrgInvitationLimit` 与 plugin-auth 的一行接入，没有数据变化。回滚就是 revert，或者干脆不设这个变量。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-limit.ts`，以及 `auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts` 里的那一处展开。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。
- 席位意见：落地。`Clause-② yes (widening)`，复审 PASS（含 delta）；CI 无失败，没有碰受管面，改动 334 行。

## 席位核对

- **形态:** draft → `main`。正文写 `Fixes #33196`，合并后应当关卡；正文其他地方没有挨着别的 open 卡号的闭合关键词。
  - 申报 `Clause-②: yes (widening)`、`Metadata-protocol: none`（不是可编写的 spec 键）；`@objectstack/plugin-auth`、`@objectstack/types` 均 patch。
  - 文件面 = 认领 6870106120 加修订（`packages/types/src/env.ts` 及其测试、新的 `invitation-limit.ts` 及其测试、组织插件一行接入、`environment-variables.mdx` 一行、changeset），7 个文件都在其中。
